slides.title: Your consulting logo doesn't need to [look clever].
slides.lede: It needs to tell a buyer whose thinking they are reading, including on documents you cannot personally explain.

slides.title: Looking suitable is not the same as [being identifiable]

cards.label: Suitable
cards.text: Does the material look right for the work we sell?

cards.label: Identifiable
cards.text: Does it clearly identify our firm, not several possible publishers?

slides.title: Can a forwarded slide [name its author]?
slides.text: Put your research chart beside a competitor's and remove the report covers. Can a reader still identify the publisher from a visible name and a recognisable treatment?

slides.title: Wordmark, monogram or symbol: [match the situation]

items.title: New firm, unknown name
items.text: Full-name wordmark, so buyers learn the name.

items.title: Clients already use your initials
items.text: Monogram supported by the full name.

items.title: Long founder name
items.text: Primary wordmark plus a compact secondary lockup.

items.title: Recognised mark, inconsistent documents
items.text: Keep the mark, repair the application system.

slides.title: Ask every designer for [the same proof sheet]
slides.note: Use realistic content. **Placeholder text tells you very little** about a long consultancy name beside a procurement reference.

slides.title: Fix the [templates] before you replace the logo
slides.text: If buyers recognise your name and mark but each partner publishes a different-looking deck, the problem is the system, not the artwork.

slides.title: Check one proposal, one report and one slide today.
slides.lede: Your consulting firm logo doesn't need to look clever. Read the full guide via the link in our bio.
